data.one_liner: A routing package built on top of Router and Navigator's pages API, supporting arbitrary nested navigation.
data.what_it_does: Beamer splits navigation responsibilities into multiple BeamLocation classes that manage stacks of pages. It integrates with Flutter's Router API to handle deep linking, nested navigation, guards, and browser history synchronization.
use_when: You need complex, nested routing structures in a Flutter application
You want declarative navigation based on page stacks and URL paths
avoid_when: You prefer simple imperative navigation like standard Navigator push and pop
You want a zero-configuration routing setup without defining location builders or route maps
strengths: Supports arbitrary nested navigation and multiple beamers
Handles deep linking and browser history out of the box
Allows modular organization of page stacks via BeamLocation
weaknesses: Steeper learning curve compared to imperative navigation or simpler routers
Requires understanding of Router and Navigator 2.0 concepts
data.setup_notes: Requires setting up MaterialApp.router with BeamerDelegate, RouteInformationParser, and BeamerBackButtonDispatcher.

alternatives.name: go_router
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a more declarative URL-based routing API officially recommended by the Flutter team.

alternatives.name: auto_route
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers code-generation-based strongly-typed routing and deep-linking support.
